name: Opus-fleet small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Concentrated long book in small/mid-cap cloud, AI-infra, and fintech compounders with secular demand, riding small-cap and software leadership while avoiding weak crypto.

positions.thesis: Now the best risk/reward in the software half of the book and promoted to joint-largest on that basis. The stock fell about 7.6% into $235.62 while 46 analysts sit at $285.18, so headroom roughly doubled from 11% to 21% purely because the price came down, and it did so on multiple compression rather than any new company-specific news: the FY26 guide is still $4.45-4.47bn on 36% revenue growth and the one-large-AI-customer usage scare was disclosed back at the 6 August print. It rose 1.32% Friday alongside an IGV bounce attributed to AI-displacement fears subsiding. I add only two points rather than backing up the truck because the long end is still at its highs with TLT on a 52-week low, which is the exact condition that compressed the multiple in the first place, and because the customer-concentration overhang is a genuine single-counterparty exposure that can produce another gap. Stop deliberately held wide at -20% rather than tightened, because that gap risk is the reason I have not sized this larger and a tight stop would simply convert a gap into a realised loss.

Held at 15% because the only new fact is calendar, not fundamental, and the calendar still favours waiting. At $230.57 it trades 37.5x forward against FY27 guidance calling for over 80% revenue growth with optical alone above $600m, which makes it the cheapest thing I own on a growth-adjusted basis even though it is the highest-beta line at 3.23. Revenue tripled to $1.34bn and net income is up 805%; 19 analysts average $283.23 with TD Cowen and Barclays both at $300, and the stock is 25% below its $308.67 high. The 1 September print is the largest single gap risk in the book, but it falls after next Saturday's reassessment, so I keep one more scheduled opportunity to cut size into it and I am not paying spread now to insure an event I can still address in time. Stop stays at -25%, the widest in the book, because at beta 3.23 anything tighter is noise rather than protection. I have moved the take-profit down from +45% to +35%, which lands near $311 just above the 52-week high, so the exit sits at a level I would genuinely want to sell into rather than at a price the stock has never seen.

Weight untouched because it is doing precisely the job I bought it for, but the stop tightens because it is now the most extended line I own. At $165.73 it is within 2.3% of its $169.68 52-week high and up 86.6% over the year against the 76.6% it showed when I sized it, and it closed green again Friday. The driver remains M&A and improving regulatory sentiment across 156 equal-weighted names at beta 0.83, which is genuinely orthogonal to the AI capex cycle that CRDO, DDOG and NET all key off, and market commentary now explicitly describes rotation out of technology into healthcare. I do not add, because the very thing that makes this line valuable is that it is uncorrelated, and pushing it larger after an 86% run converts a diversifier into a momentum bet. Stop tightened from -15% to -12% for one reason: biotech gives back fast, this is the only holding sitting on a 52-week high, and with the 30-year brushing 5% the sector still carries duration that a hawkish surprise would hit.

Restored to a full-size line because I was wrong to cut it and the reason it worked is structural rather than a one-day headline. All three revenue engines are now firing at once: Trump's push for the Clarity Act took BTC to roughly $72,475 and drove HOOD up 13.7% in a session with COIN up 8.2% alongside, prediction markets grew revenue tenfold in a quarter, and with TLT sitting on its 52-week low and the 30-year near 5% the roughly one-third of revenue that is net interest keeps compounding. That last point is why this is the leg I add to rather than the software names: it is the only holding whose earnings power improves in exactly the high-long-end regime that is compressing NET's and DDOG's multiples, which makes it a real hedge inside a long-only book rather than just another ticker. I stop at 15% instead of making it my largest position because the catalyst is a bill that has been called for and not passed, 28 analysts average only $119.93 against $108.13, and buying unlimited size the day after a 13.7% gap on a legislative headline is the mirror image of the recency error I just made in the other direction. Stop at -20% around $86.50 gives it room to hand back the entire gap and more before I am out, which at beta 2.32 is the only stop worth having; take-profit at +45% sits just above the $153.86 52-week high.

Cut three points because the specific premise I cited for the promotion has expired, not because the business changed. I wrote that I was adding into a valuation-supported breakout after it closed $15.23 back above its $15.06 200-day; at $14.58 it is below that line again, so the breakout half of that sentence is gone and the three points that rested on it come off. What remains is the half that got stronger: the 13 August print delivered the first billion-dollar net income quarter in company history at 33% ROE, it trades 15.18x forward against mid-30s growth making it comfortably the cheapest thing I own, 22 analysts average $18.69 for 28% upside, and it rose 2.60% Friday. It is also still the only holding whose earnings power is driven by Brazilian and Mexican penetration rather than US long-end rates or AI sentiment, and at beta 0.94 it is the lowest-beta name in a book where everything else is levered to one of those two factors. That is worth a 14% core. Stop stays wide at -18% because a 15x multiple provides real downside support and I refuse to be shaken out of a post-gap consolidation. Take-profit moved down from +40% to +30%, which lands around $18.95 at both the consensus target and the 52-week high, so the exit is anchored to a price the market has actually paid rather than to a number I invented.

Nudged up one point, the smallest adjustment in the book, because the complaint I made last week has been partly answered by the price. I trimmed this to the smallest line arguing that 5.6% of consensus headroom was not enough pay for carrying the highest multiple I own; the stock then fell about 7.2% to $293.14 while 34 analysts hold $333.55, so that headroom is now 13.8%, with Citi at $400 and BofA at $380 as the bull case. The business never wobbled: 33.5% revenue growth, guidance raised on AI-driven demand, FedRAMP High certification and the Kitesurf agent browser are real product momentum, and it bounced 5.10% Friday. But it is still 198x forward with a GAAP loss, and TLT pinned at a 52-week low with the 30-year near 5% means the duration pressure that caused the de-rate is still present rather than resolved, so this stays the smallest position in the book and gets one point, not four. Stop held tight at -15% around $249, the tightest in the book alongside XBI, because on a name where essentially all remaining return must come from multiple expansion the downside is exactly as fast as the multiple, and I would rather be stopped out and reassess than round-trip this.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-22: Three specific facts changed, and each one points at a different leg. First, the stated premise for NU's promotion has failed: I sized it 17% partly because it had reclaimed its $15.06 200-day at $15.23, and it is now $14.58, back underneath. When I name a reason for incremental size and that reason expires, the incremental size comes off — otherwise the reasoning is decorative. The 15.18x forward multiple and 28% consensus headroom are intact and better than a week ago, so the core stays at 14%; only the breakout premium goes. Second, I was wrong on HOOD and the correction is a legislative catalyst, not noise: Trump pushing the Clarity Act took BTC to roughly $72.5k and HOOD up 13.7% in a session. More important than the pop is that TLT is pinned at its 52-week low with the 30-year near 5%, which means high-for-longer is the live regime, and HOOD is the only line I own whose net interest income compounds in precisely the macro state that is de-rating NET and DDOG. I add three points on the hedge logic, not the momentum, and I deliberately keep it at 15% rather than making it the sole largest line, because the Act has been called for and not passed and a failed vote gives the whole gap back. Third, the de-rate I trimmed into actually happened, which mechanically improved what I am paid to carry: DDOG's headroom went from 11% to 21% and NET's from 5.6% to 13.8% because the prices fell, not because targets rose. Buying a modest amount of the discount I made room for is the point of having trimmed. I add two points to DDOG and one to NET, weighted toward DDOG because it offers half again the headroom at a far lower multiple, and I keep the adds small because IGV at -2.77% over a year with the long end still at the highs says the pressure has not lifted. CRDO and XBI are untouched on the merits: CRDO's 1 September print sits past next week's desk so there is no gap to pre-empt yet, and XBI is doing exactly the job I bought it for. Total turnover is about 14% of NAV at roughly 2bps a side, so the frictional cost of acting on this is negligible against the risk of leaving a stale rationale in place.
novelty: I run only the Round-3 book in this experiment, so there is no Round-2 sleeve to overlap with; the distinguishing feature of this book remains that its crypto exposure is expressed solely through a regulated brokerage's transaction and net-interest franchise rather than through any spot or perp leg, and that its largest diversifier is an equal-weighted biotech basket whose driver is M&A rather than the AI capex cycle every other line keys off.
research_notes:
Checked every line's mark and the macro regime rather than assuming last week's picture held.

MARKS (2026-08-21 close): NU $14.58 (+2.60% Fri), fwd P/E 15.18, 22 analysts avg $18.69 (+28%), 52wk $11.20-18.98. CRDO $230.57 (-0.34% Fri), fwd P/E 37.5, 19 analysts avg $283.23 (+22.8%), TD Cowen and Barclays both $300, 52wk $86.49-308.67, EARNINGS 1 SEPTEMBER. XBI $165.73 (+1.44% Fri), 52wk $88.23-169.68 so within 2.3% of its high, +86.6% 1yr (was +76.6% when I bought it). DDOG $235.62 (+1.32% Fri), 46 analysts avg $285.18 (+21.0%), 52wk $98.01-292.72. HOOD $108.13, +13.7% on Friday alone, 28 analysts avg $119.93 (+10.9%), 52wk $63.52-153.86. NET $293.14 (+5.10% Fri), fwd P/E 198.4, 34 analysts avg $333.55 (+13.8%), Citi $400 / BofA $380.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED. The de-rate I positioned for last week landed: NET fell from $315.78 to $293.14 (-7.2%) and DDOG from roughly $255 to $235.62 (-7.6%), while XBI and the small-cap complex made new highs. Trimming NET and DDOG and adding to XBI was correct. The one thing I got wrong was HOOD: I cut it three points calling it a laggard and it then gained 13.7% in a session.

THE CRYPTO EVENT, VERIFIED. The move was not spontaneous. Trump publicly called on Congress to pass the Clarity Act (digital-asset regulatory framework); BTC jumped ~4.6% to about $72,475, roughly +12% over two sessions off the low-$60ks. COIN +8.2% to $186.49, HOOD +13.7%. I hold no spot crypto and no perps, so no standing order of mine fired — my exposure to this is entirely through HOOD's transaction franchise, which is the form I want it in (no 35bps spot spread, no funding, and it comes bundled with prediction markets and net interest income).

THE RATE REGIME IS THE KEY DIVERGENCE. TLT closed $82.05, sitting on its 52-week low of $81.17, with the 30-year brushing 5%. So the long end is NOT relieved even though equities rallied Friday. That matters because it means the duration pressure on 198x-forward NET and on DDOG has not gone away — the group de-rated and the cause is still present. IGV confirms the group is the laggard: $103.37, -2.77% over one year, 12.4% below its 52-week high, though it bounced 1.43% Friday on commentary that AI-displacement fears are subsiding. Meanwhile IWM $299.96 is 1.7% from its high, +34% over a year, and SPY $765.72 is 1.8% off its high. Small-cap leadership, my mandate's tailwind, is intact.

The synthesis: a high-long-end regime is a headwind for my two software lines and a direct tailwind for HOOD's net interest income. HOOD is therefore the only holding whose earnings power improves in the exact macro state that hurts the rest of the book — a real hedge, not a coincidence of tickers.

CRDO TIMING. Its print is 1 September, which falls after next Saturday's desk, so I retain one more reassessment to manage the gap. I am not pre-trimming a 22.8% headroom name a week and a half early.
